_comment: Copy this file to config.json and fill in your family. config.json is gitignored. The reasoning model is configured in OpenClaw, not here — Homebase is model-agnostic and works with whichever model OpenClaw is set to.

location._comment: Used for weather lookups (Open-Meteo, no key required) and timezone-aware scheduling.

whatsapp._comment: The primary family group is groups[0] — used by the morning briefing, school email monitor, and meal check-in. agent_number is the phone the bridge sends from. Legacy shape (group_id scalar) is still accepted by config_loader for backward compat, but new configs should use groups[].

alerts._comment: Out-of-band failure channel for the claude-runners, surfaced by get_message_targets as alert_webhook and used by notify_out_of_band in claude-runners/_lib/runner.sh when a WhatsApp alert cannot be delivered. It must NOT route through the OpenClaw gateway: every other runner send already does, which makes the gateway a single point of failure for both a message and the warning that the message did not go. A plain HTTPS push (ntfy.sh, or any URL that accepts a POST body) still reaches you when the gateway is what broke. Carries the failure reason only, never message content, so a public relay is acceptable. Leave empty to disable.

calendar._comment: id is the Google Calendar ID (looks like ...@group.calendar.google.com or 'primary'). primary_email_id is your personal Gmail used to filter out personal calendar events from the family briefing.
calendar.name: Family Calendar

supported_calendars._comment: Optional list of additional Google Calendars to merge in (e.g. a work calendar shared as free/busy-only with your personal Google account). All entries are read using the same OAuth token as calendar.id above — no separate credentials needed as long as the calendar is shared with that account. Each entry needs: name, type ('google'), id (the calendar ID — often the owner's email for a shared primary calendar), enabled.
supported_calendars.name: Family Calendar

family._comment: members is a list of {name, phone}; both formats (list and phone-keyed dict) are accepted. kids has per-child structured meals and an emoji ('boy'/'girl' map to 👦/👧, anything else to 🧒). Each kid may have 'email_sender' — the teacher/admin email that sends school updates for THIS child specifically. The school email monitor uses this to attribute incoming emails to the right kid; the value must exactly match the From: address (case-insensitive). The 'meals' object has three slots (breakfast, lunch, sides), each with an 'options' array of concrete menu items the planner is allowed to pick from. A slot may instead use 'fixed_dish' + 'rotate_grains' (e.g. always khichdi, rotate the grain). Optional 'constraints' is a list of named rules — currently only 'no_eggs_at_lunch_if_eggs_at_breakfast' is recognized. Items are added incrementally over time via the catalog learning flow; you don't need to enumerate everything up front.

stores._comment: Used by the shopping list to group items by store. Add as many keys as you want; the morning briefing knows about indian/bulk/general but the shopping list will route to any key here.

school._comment: email_domains and email_addresses build the Gmail search query for the school email monitor. List EVERY domain the school can mail from, including its software vendor's — these are often several, and they are not guessable from each other. Procare, for example, sends day-to-day messages from one domain and calendar/event invitations from a different one. A sender that is not listed is never fetched, which is silent in a way a dropped email is not: there is no log line anywhere, because nothing was ever read.
school.name: School Name

bills._comment: Watches Gmail for bill mail from the given billers within lookback_days. Where a PDF statement is attached its text is extracted via pypdf; where it is not, the email body is used instead, because plenty of billers only ever send a 'your bill is ready, log in to view' notice with nothing attached. Prints structured JSON on stdout for the caller to summarize (consumption + genuine tips pulled from the bill's own content) and post to the primary family WhatsApp group (whatsapp.groups[0]) — one of the jobs permitted to target the family group under CLAUDE.md principle 6. Errors/empty polls stay silent on the group and DM the owner instead, same silence-or-substance contract as the school email monitor. 'sender' is a full mailbox address, not just a domain — some billers send through a shared third-party billing platform, so matching on domain alone could pull in unrelated senders. It must also be the address the INVOICE arrives from: billers commonly send invoices and payment receipts from two different mailboxes, and configuring the receipt one means no bill is ever matched. Find it by searching your own inbox for a past bill and copying the exact From: address. lookback_days must comfortably exceed the longest gap between scheduled runs, or mail arriving just after one run ages out before the next. Non-bill mail from these addresses (outage alerts, marketing, receipts) is matched too and is expected to be recognized and dropped downstream. Set enabled to true once billers[] has at least one real sender.

briefing._comment: Time the morning briefing fires (24h). weather and positive_message are feature flags.
